Das OEG ist seit dem 1. Januar 2024 im S.en: Since 1 January 2024, the Victim Compensation Act (Opferentschädigungsgesetz, OEG) has been incorporated into Book XIV of the Social Code (SGB XIV). What this means for ongoing proceedings and old decisions.

Das OEG gibt es so nicht mehr.en: The OEG no longer exists in this form

Das Opferentschädigungsgesetz wurde zum.en: With effect from 1 January 2024, the Victim Compensation Act (Opferentschädigungsgesetz) was replaced by Book XIV of the Social Code (Vierzehntes Buch Sozialgesetzbuch, SGB XIV). Since then, this area has been called social compensation law (Soziales Entschädigungsrecht), and all new applications go through it.

Der Begriff „OEG\" ist trotzdem gebliebe.en: Even so, the term “OEG” has stuck — in official decisions, at advice centres and in people’s minds. Anyone who knows it will also search for it. That is why this page explains what it still means today.

Wann das alte Recht noch gilt.en: When the old law still applies

Für Anträge, die vor dem 1. Januar 2024.en: Applications made before 1 January 2024 continue to be assessed under the OEG. So an ongoing procedure does not switch its legal basis halfway through.

Wer vor 2024 bereits Leistungen bezogen.en: Anyone who was already receiving benefits before 2024 was automatically transferred to the new law. The decisions remain valid, the payments continued without interruption, and no new application was needed for this.

Ein Blick auf den alten Bescheid kann si.en: It can be worth taking a look at your old decision

Wer durch eine Gewalttat gesundheitliche.en: Anyone who has suffered damage to their health as a result of an act of violence can receive social compensation benefits (Leistungen der Sozialen Entschädigung). Since 1 January 2024, this has been governed by Book XIV of the Social Code (SGB XIV), which replaced the Victim Compensation Act (Opferentschädigungsgesetz).

Der Gedanke dahinter: Der Staat konnte d.en: The idea behind it: the state was unable to prevent the crime and therefore takes responsibility for its consequences. This is not about damages from the perpetrator — that route remains unaffected.

Das ist die wichtigste Neuerung gegenübe.en: This is the most important change compared with the OEG. The old law required a physical assault (tätlicher Angriff) — that is, physical violence. In addition, SGB XIV also covers serious psychological violence, such as significant threats or stalking (Nachstellungen) with consequences for health.

Wer früher deshalb abgelehnt wurde oder.en: If you were turned down for this reason in the past, or never applied in the first place, you should raise the question again.

Die Traumaambulanz — Hilfe, bevor irgend.en: The trauma outpatient clinic (Traumaambulanz) — help before anything has been decided

Möglich sind bis zu 15 Sitzungen. Die er.en: Up to 15 sessions are possible. The first should take place within twelve months of the crime; if the crime was longer ago, the twelve months count from when the acute distress first appeared. Travel costs and accompanying persons are covered.

Wird der Antrag später abgelehnt, musst.en: If the application is later rejected, you do not have to pay back the costs of the trauma outpatient clinic (Traumaambulanz).

Zuständig sind die Versorgungsbehörden d.en: The pension offices of the federal states (Versorgungsbehörden der Bundesländer) are responsible. There is no deadline for applying — so the crime may also have happened a long time ago.

Wichtig ist trotzdem der Zeitpunkt: Leis.en: The timing still matters, though: benefits are generally only provided from the date of application, not retroactively. If you are thinking about whether to apply, every month you wait costs you benefits you would otherwise have received.

Ein Monat für den Widerspruch.en: One month to lodge an objection (Widerspruch)

Gegen einen Bescheid kannst du innerhalb.en: You can lodge an objection (Widerspruch) against a decision within one month of being notified of it. The deadline runs even if you are still waiting for documents — a short objection that meets the deadline is enough at first; you can submit the reasons later.

Du musst das nicht allein durchstehen.en: You don’t have to go through this alone

Ein Antragsverfahren im Entschädigungsre.en: An application procedure under compensation law often takes years and requires you to describe the crime again and again. Wie der GdB festgestellt wird, wann es e.en: How the degree of disability (Grad der Behinderung, GdB) is determined, when you get a severe disability card (Schwerbehindertenausweis) and how long it takes.

Der Grad der Behinderung beschreibt, wie.en: The degree of disability (Grad der Behinderung) describes how strongly health impairments affect participation in life in society. It is determined in steps of ten from 20 to 100.

Ab einem GdB von 50 gilt man als schwerb.en: With a GdB of 50 or more, you are considered severely disabled and receive a severe disability card (Schwerbehindertenausweis). Compensatory entitlements (Nachteilsausgleiche) are linked to it — from protection against dismissal to tax allowances.

Der GdB ist kein Prozentwert und keine A.en: The GdB is not a percentage and says nothing about a person’s worth. It is an administrative measure to which rights are attached.

Beantragt wird die Feststellung, nicht d.en: What you apply for is the determination, not the card

Das klingt nach Wortklauberei, ist aber.en: This sounds like splitting hairs, but it is the core of the procedure: at the pension office (Versorgungsamt), you apply for a determination of disability under Section 152 of Book IX of the Social Code (§ 152 SGB IX). The card only follows if the result is a GdB of at least 50.

Das Amt fordert die Befunde bei den beha.en: The office requests the medical findings from your treating doctors and assesses them according to the Principles of Medical Care (Versorgungsmedizinische Grundsätze). A personal examination usually does not take place.

Die Bearbeitung dauert je nach Bundeslan.en: Processing usually takes two to six months, depending on the federal state and the case. The determination applies retroactively to the month in which the application was made — so applying early is never a mistake.

Wie andere Verfahren ausgegangen sind.en: How other cases have turned out

Ob sich ein Widerspruch lohnt, lässt sic.en: Whether an objection (Widerspruch) is worthwhile is easier to judge if you know of comparable cases. Antrag bei der Pflegekasse, Begutachtung.en: Application to the long-term care insurance fund (Pflegekasse), assessment by the Medical Service (Medizinischer Dienst) and the 25-working-day deadline.

Die Pflegeversicherung kennt die Pflegeg.en: Long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung) has care levels (Pflegegrade) 1 to 5. The yardstick is not a diagnosis but independence: what can someone still do on their own, and what do they need help with?

Begutachtet werden dabei ausdrücklich au.en: The assessment explicitly also covers psychological impairments and behaviours — not just physical limitations. This is often underestimated.

Der Antrag geht an die Pflegekasse, die.en: The application goes to the long-term care insurance fund (Pflegekasse), which is based at your own health insurance fund (Krankenkasse). It can be made informally — in writing, online, by phone or in person. A single sentence is enough to start with.

Die Pflegekasse beauftragt dann den Medi.en: The long-term care insurance fund (Pflegekasse) then instructs the Medical Service (Medizinischer Dienst) to carry out the assessment. It usually takes place at home and looks at your everyday life.

Von der Antragstellung bis zum Bescheid.en: As a rule, the long-term care insurance fund (Pflegekasse) has 25 working days from the application to the decision. Together with the decision, you can request the assessment report — if you want to lodge an objection, you need it.

Ein Pflegetagebuch hilft bei der Begutac.en: A care diary (Pflegetagebuch) helps with the assessment

Der Begutachtungstermin ist eine Momenta.en: The assessment appointment is a snapshot, and on bad days in particular it is hard to describe your own everyday life. If you spend one to two weeks beforehand noting down what you needed help with and how long it took, you have something concrete to go on.

Wenn der Pflegegrad zu niedrig ausfällt.en: If the care level turns out too low

Das kommt vor, und es liegt nicht immer.en: This happens, and it is not always down to the assessment: a good day, a composed, orderly impression or the habit of not letting anything show can skew the picture.

Fordere zuerst das Gutachten an und lies.en: First request the assessment report and read what was evaluated in it. There is often a point where something is missing or was assessed as better than it is — that is your starting point for the objection (Widerspruch).

Ziel: Wir erfassen anonymisiert und bund.en: Aim: We record, anonymously and state by state, structural shortcomings as well as best practices in how social compensation law (Soziales Entschädigungsrecht, SER; formerly the Crime Victims Compensation Act, OEG, now Book XIV of the Social Code, SGB XIV) is applied. Ziel: Im Zentrum steht ein systematisch.en: Aim: At the centre is a systematically developed set of questions to the state offices (Landesämter) about how OEG/SGB XIV procedures are implemented in the federal states, how they run and how transparent they are. We collect structural data in order to improve how the law is applied in the long term and to make targeted political influence possible.

Unsere Veranstaltungen zum Fonds Sexuell.en: Our events on the Fund for Sexual Abuse (Fonds Sexueller Missbrauch, FSM)

Die plötzlichen Veränderungen beim Fonds.en: The sudden changes to the Fund for Sexual Abuse (FSM) did not just unsettle many survivors – they shook their trust.

Neue Fristen, Jahrestranchen, der Wegfal.en: New deadlines, annual instalments, the end of advance payments and complicated transitional rules were hard enough to understand as early as the beginning of 2025. Many survivors suddenly no longer knew which rule applied to them, what could still be applied for and how benefits that had already been approved could still be used at all.

Deshalb haben wir mehrere kostenfreie On.en: That is why we offered several free online events on “FSM vs. open questions”. We did not just want to pass on information, but to sort out what had become confusing because of so many new rules. Together we looked at when an approval had been granted, which deadlines applied, which instalments were affected and what had actually changed.

Aus diesen Veranstaltungen entstanden da.en: These events then gave rise to our “help with filling in new applications”, which we also offered several times free of charge. We went through the applications together step by step, answered questions and tried to turn a stressful and complicated procedure into something that felt a little less overwhelming, working towards the application deadline of 31 August 2025.

Wir machten Mut, wir motivierten, wir ha.en: We encouraged people, we motivated them, we helped them submit new applications.

Plötzlich gab der FSM bekannt, dass Erst.en: Suddenly the FSM announced that, retroactively, first applications would only be considered if they had been received by 19 March 2025 – even though a much later application deadline, 31 August 2025, had been used until then – and that no further new applications were possible from then on.

Für viele Betroffene war das mehr als ei.en: For many survivors this was more than a shock!

Wir waren erschüttert und schämten uns,.en: We were shaken and ashamed that after 19 March 2025 we had still motivated and supported so many survivors to submit this stressful application, which was now no longer accepted.

Menschen haben ihren Mut zusammengenomme.en: People had plucked up their courage, gone back over their own story, gathered documents and filled in applications – often under great psychological strain. And then they had to learn that their application would no longer be considered because of a cut-off date set retroactively.

Auch wir waren darüber enttäuscht, wüten.en: We too were disappointed, angry and stunned. Because a support system for people who have experienced severe violence, of all things, should act reliably, transparently and in a trauma-sensitive way – and not add the feeling of once again having no control and being let down once again.

Aus einer geplanten Ausfüllhilfe-Veranst.en: So a planned session to help with the application became a space for “frustration and questions”. Everything was allowed there: disappointment, anger, uncertainty, open questions and worries about what would happen next. At the same time, we looked together at which options still existed and how survivors could continue to assert their rights.

So setzten wir im November 2025 unsere V.en: We continued our events in November 2025. Under the motto “We will not be silenced – we keep fighting!” we gave information on new developments, existing support options and the further winding-up of the fund.

Bei allen diesen Veranstaltungen war uns.en: At all of these events it was particularly important to us that nobody had to overcome additional hurdles: free of charge, no membership, no need to give your real name, camera and microphone optional, and questions possible via the chat at any time.

Unsere FSM-Veranstaltungen waren deshalb.en: Our FSM events were therefore much more than information evenings. They were places to understand, sort things out, be supported, ask questions and be heard.

Und sie haben uns noch einmal sehr deutl.en: And they showed us once again very clearly: help must not itself become the next burden. Whoever promises support must also make sure that people can rely on that support.

Falls du einen Ablehnungsbescheid zum be.en: If you have received a rejection notice regarding disability-related additional needs or your new application after 19 March 2025, you can lodge an objection. You will find templates for the objection and our statements on our [page on the Fund for Sexual Abuse](/fsm-erweitertes-hilfesystem#dokumente).

Zusammenarbeit mit aus-unserer-sicht im.en: Cooperation with aus-unserer-sicht on social compensation law: SGB XIV / OEG

*KE!N EINZELFALL e.V.* hatte die Möglich.en: *KE!N EINZELFALL e.V.* had the opportunity, within the working groups of *aus-unserer-sicht e.V.*, to work intensively on social compensation law, and in particular on the change from the OEG to SGB XIV and the implementation of SGB XIV.

Unsere 1. Vorsitzende Tatjana Belmar nah.en: Our chair Tatjana Belmar took an active part in the *working group on social compensation law (AG SER)*. The working group focused on survivors’ experiences with the previous victims’ compensation law and the new social compensation law, and on how procedures could be made more survivor-centred, more transparent and less stressful.

Ein wichtiger Bestandteil dieser Zusamme.en: An important part of this cooperation was the conference day in November 2024. There, Tatjana Belmar ran the workshop *“SGB XIV – a first evaluation of social compensation law from our point of view!”* for KE!N EINZELFALL e.V.

Im Workshop wurden gemeinsam Erfahrungen.en: In the workshop, participants looked together at experiences with the transition from the OEG to SGB XIV. Topics included application procedures, bureaucratic processes, changes brought by the new law, existing hurdles and survivors’ positive and negative experiences. The aim was to make experiential knowledge visible and to derive feedback and possible improvements for the further implementation of social compensation law.

Aus der Arbeit in der AG entwickelte sic.en: The work in the group then gave rise to the idea of a follow-up project. The plan was a nationwide, anonymised and structured evaluation of experiences and documents from OEG/SGB XIV proceedings. The aim was not to assess individual cases, but to make recurring patterns of best practice and worst case visible.

Untersucht werden sollten insbesondere:\.en:
The project was to look in particular at:
- structural shortcomings and procedural errors,
- differences between the federal states,
- experiences with expert reports and assessment procedures,
- deadlines and processing procedures,
- examples of good practice,
- and ways of better preparing the support system for the needs of survivors.

Für dieses Vorhaben sollte zunächst ein.en: For this, a sound survey and project plan was first to be developed. This included developing evaluation categories, questions of anonymisation and data protection, securing the legal basis for using the data, and planning the later evaluation and publication.

In die Überlegungen flossen auch bereits.en: The planning also drew on existing experience and preparatory work by KE!N EINZELFALL e.V., including existing contacts with survivors and prepared requests under the Freedom of Information Act.

Das langfristige Ziel war, Erfahrungen n.en: The long-term goal was not only to collect experiences, but to derive concrete findings about structural problems and working solutions. These were then to be passed on to, among others, the responsible state authorities, victims’ commissioners, federal ministries and institutions of the support system.

*aus-unserer-sicht e.V. löste sich zum 1.en: *aus-unserer-sicht e.V. was dissolved as of 11 February 2026*, so the planned cooperation and the project that had been worked out could not be continued in this form. KE!N EINZELFALL e.V. has continued parts of the project on its own.

Trotzdem war diese Zeit für uns sehr wer.en: Even so, this time was very valuable for us. We were able to gain experience, network with other survivors and committed people, get to know different perspectives and develop our own work in social compensation law.

*Wir danken aus-unserer-sicht e.V. für d.en: *We thank aus-unserer-sicht e.V. for the opportunity to take part, for the experiences we shared and for the space in which survivors’ knowledge could be contributed and developed further.*

Auch wenn dieses Projekt nicht gemeinsam.en: Even though this project could not be completed together, the experience gained and many of the ideas that came out of it remain part of our ongoing work.

ANUAS-Arbeitsgruppe „Mit-Opferrechte“: K.en: ANUAS working group “Co-victims’ rights”: KE!N EINZELFALL e.V. brings the expertise of those affected into the expert dialogue on victim protection, co-victims and social compensation law.

Was brauchen Opfer und Mit-Opfer nach sc.en: What do victims and co-victims really need after serious violence – and what happens when support systems exist, but those affected still cannot find reliable access to support within them?

Im Rahmen der *ANUAS-Arbeitsgruppe „Mit-.en: As part of the *ANUAS working group “Co-victims’ rights” (Mit-Opferrechte)* we bring our experience from victim support and our lived expertise into the professional exchange. We look at how victim protection, social compensation law, medical and psychotherapeutic care and institutional procedures can be designed so that they actually support those affected – instead of burdening them further through complicated procedures, unclear responsibilities or a lack of trauma sensitivity.

Unser Ziel ist ein Hilfesystem, in dem *.en: Our goal is a support system in which *people talk not only about those affected, but with them.*

Unsere Stellungnahme zum Fachdialog „Mit.en: Our statement on the expert dialogue “Co-victims’ rights”

Nach dem Fachdialog der ANUAS-Arbeitsgru.en: After the expert dialogue of the ANUAS working group on 13 October 2026, we summarised our positions once more in a statement of our own.

Für uns steht dabei besonders im Mittelp.en: For us, one point is central: *Trauma sensitivity must not depend on the personal commitment of individual professionals. It has to become part of professional standards.*

Gewalterfahrungen können langfristige Au.en: Experiences of violence can have long-term effects on mental and physical health, relationships, the ability to work, social participation and the whole of a person’s life. These connections must be taken into account in care, assessments and social law procedures.

Genauso wichtig ist uns, dass Betroffene.en: It is just as important to us that those affected are not seen merely as *a file, a diagnosis or a person in need of help*. Despite – and sometimes precisely because of – their experiences, people bring knowledge, skills, resources and competences with them.

Deshalb setzen wir uns für eine Unterstü.en: That is why we advocate support that does not only look at deficits, but *strengthens self-determination and existing resources*.

Aus unserer Arbeit und den Diskussionen.en: From our work and the discussions within the working group, we have formulated concrete demands for improving care and institutional victim protection.

Dazu gehören insbesondere:\n- verbindlic.en:
These include in particular:
- mandatory trauma sensitivity in training, further training and continuing education,
- a holistic view of the long-term consequences of violence,
- understandable and transparent procedures,
- protection against institutional secondary victimisation,
- better transitions between therapy and care,
- closer networking between psychotherapy, psychiatry, rehabilitation, social benefit agencies and victim support,
- guides and qualified support through complicated procedures,
- and the systematic involvement of people with their own experience of violence.

Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt liegt auf der.en: One particular focus is the question: *How can institutions check whether their procedures actually work for those affected?*

Deshalb setzen wir uns für eine *Betroff.en: That is why we advocate an *impact assessment from the perspective of those affected* (Betroffenenverträglichkeitsprüfung).

Nicht nur Gesetze und Verwaltungsabläufe.en: Laws and administrative processes must not only be formally correct. It must also be examined *what effect they have in reality on the people they were created for.*

Fachdialog der ANUAS-Arbeitsgruppe „Mit-.en: Expert dialogue of the ANUAS working group “Co-victims’ rights”

Am 13. Oktober 2026 nehmen wir erneut am.en: On 13 October 2026 we are once again taking part in the expert dialogue of the ANUAS working group *“Co-victims’ rights”*.

Ausgangspunkt ist unter anderem ein lauf.en: One starting point is an ongoing petition procedure by the federal association ANUAS e.V. on the situation of co-victims of homicides.

Dabei geht es nicht nur um einzelne Leis.en:
This is not just about individual benefits. The focus is on fundamental questions:
- Are victims’ rights actually achieved in practice?
- Does social compensation law work for the people who depend on it?
- Where do authorities and institutions create additional burdens?
- How can co-victims be better recognised and supported?
- And how can those affected themselves be involved in developing these systems further?

Auch die Umsetzung und Evaluation des SG.en: The implementation and evaluation of SGB XIV, official investigation, the design of procedures, trauma-sensitive application guidelines and the involvement of organisations of those affected are also discussed.

Schreiben des BMAS wird zum Ausgangspunk.en: Letter from the BMAS becomes the starting point for further discussions

Im Zusammenhang mit den Anliegen von ANU.en: In connection with the concerns raised by ANUAS, the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs states that questions about the situation of co-victims have already been examined several times – among other things in connection with the legislative procedure for SGB XIV. Statements submitted as part of the consultation of associations had also been examined.

Aus Sicht des Ministeriums habe sich dar.en: In the ministry’s view, however, this had not resulted in any further mandate for action.

Für die Arbeitsgruppe wird genau dies zu.en: For the working group, this is exactly what becomes an important starting point: *Is it enough that a problem has been examined – or must we also look at whether the existing rules actually work in practice?*

Gerade diese Frage beschäftigt uns immer.en: This question keeps coming back to us.

Ein besonders prägender Moment der Arbei.en: A particularly formative moment for the working group is the account of a married couple who lost their son in a terrorist attack in Hamburg. What they describe makes clear how far-reaching the consequences of a violent crime can be for relatives too.

It is not only about grief. It is about:
- psychological and physical consequences,
- financial changes,
- limitations on the ability to work,
- finding one’s way in social compensation law,
- therapeutic support,
- dealing with authorities,
- and the question of who actually helps to connect all these different systems.

Besonders deutlich wird: *Mit-Opfer könn.en: It becomes particularly clear: *After a serious violent crime, co-victims often cannot simply do their own research, submit applications, clarify responsibilities and find their way through different support systems.*

Gerade in dieser Situation braucht es Un.en: Especially in this situation, people need support, orientation and reliable contacts.

Unsere Auseinandersetzung mit dem Sozial.en: Our work on social compensation law

Aus dem Austausch heraus beschäftigen wi.en: Building on this exchange, we are looking closely at the possibilities and limits of the *OEG and SGB XIV*.

Wir schauen unter anderem auf:\n- Entsch.en:

- needs assessment,

They need:

Wenn ein Recht an der Suche nach Sachver.en: When a right fails because no expert can be found

§ 109 SGG: Betroffene dürfen im Sozialge.en: § 109 SGG: in social court proceedings, those affected may name a doctor of their choice, but can hardly find any experts. KE!N EINZELFALL e.V. documents the search and the replies.

Im Sozialen Entschädigungsrecht können G.en: In social compensation law, expert opinions can play a decisive role in whether experiences of violence and their health consequences are recognised.

Im sozialgerichtlichen Verfahren gibt *§.en: In proceedings before the social courts, *§ 109 SGG* gives those affected the option of applying for a doctor of their choice to be heard as an expert. Especially after an expert opinion that went against them, this option can be of great importance.

In der Praxis sind wir jedoch auf eine g.en: In practice, however, we came up against a fundamental difficulty: *Those affected have to name a suitable expert – but, especially for questions of testimony credibility, they can hardly find anyone who meets the professional requirements and actually accepts such an assignment.*

Aus einem konkreten Problem entstand des.en: A concrete problem therefore turned into a larger research and awareness project.

Unser Ziel ist es herauszufinden:\n- Wo.en:
Our aim is to find out:
- Where can those affected find suitable experts?
- Who is responsible for providing reliable guidance?
- What is happening with the register of expert assessors provided for by law in social compensation law?
- And how can a right under § 109 SGG actually be used if access to suitable professionals is hardly possible in practice?

Auch Monate nach Beginn unserer bundeswe.en: Even months after our nationwide research began, the question of actual access to suitable experts has not been finally resolved.

Auf eine unserer Anfragen teilt uns das.en: In response to one of our enquiries, the *Augsburg Social Court* informs us that it cannot answer the questions itself and cannot send any lists of experts. Our enquiry is therefore forwarded to the *Bavarian Higher Social Court*.

Für uns zeigt auch diese Rückmeldung ern.en: For us, this response once again shows the fundamental problem: *Those affected are passed from one office to the next, while they themselves have to name a specific expert to the court.*

Erneute Antwort des Bundesministeriums f.en: Another reply from the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs

Nach unserer weiteren Nachfrage erhalten.en: After a further enquiry, we again receive a written reply from the *Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (BMAS)*. The ministry confirms once more that it will create a register of expert assessors.

Gleichzeitig weist das BMAS darauf hin,.en: At the same time, the BMAS points out that such a register could only provide information about the *suitability* of expert assessors – not about whether they are actually available or could take on an assignment.

Zur eigenen Suche verweist das BMAS Betr.en:
For their own search, the BMAS continues to refer those affected to, among others:
- medical associations,
- professional associations,
- and lawyers specialising in social law.

Für uns bleibt damit eine entscheidende.en: For us, a crucial question therefore remains open: *How is a person affected supposed to make practical use of a legal right if they have to name an expert themselves, but no central office can say who is actually available for such an assignment?*

Die Antwort des BMAS vom Juli klärt für.en: The BMAS reply from July clarifies for us for the first time who will be responsible for the register of expert assessors in future. However, it does not solve the actual problem.

Deshalb fragen wir erneut nach: Was bede.en: That is why we ask again: What does a future register mean for those affected who need an expert *now*?

Wie soll der Zugang konkret funktioniere.en: How is access supposed to work in concrete terms?

Und wie wird verhindert, dass ein gesetz.en: And how is it to be prevented that a statutory procedural right fails in practice because nobody can be found?

BMAS bestätigt: Das vorgesehene Gutachte.en: BMAS confirms: the planned register of expert assessors does not yet exist

Das Bundesministerium für Arbeit und Soz.en: The Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs answers our renewed enquiry in writing. In doing so, we receive a confirmation that is particularly important for our project: until the end of June 2026, the *Federal Office for Social Compensation* was responsible for keeping a register of medical expert assessors experienced in social compensation law.

Das BMAS teilt uns jedoch ausdrücklich m.en: However, the BMAS expressly informs us: *No such register had been created by then.* When the task passed to the BMAS in July 2026, there was therefore no existing register to take over.

Das Ministerium erklärt, dass nun umfang.en: The ministry explains that extensive research is now under way to create a register of expert assessors. It could not yet say at this point when the register would be publicly accessible.

Damit bestätigt sich eine unserer zentra.en: This confirms one of our central observations: *An orientation tool for those affected that is provided for by law was not available in practice for a long period of time.*

Im Laufe unserer Recherche wird deutlich.en: In the course of our research it becomes clear that responsibility for the register of expert assessors is also changing.

Die Aufgabe war ursprünglich in *§ 124 A.en: The task was originally assigned to the Federal Office for Social Compensation in *§ 124 (4) no. 5 SGB XIV*. In the course of legislative changes, however, the task is removed there or reassigned.

Für Betroffene entsteht dadurch zunächst.en: For those affected, this initially creates additional uncertainty: *Who will actually keep the register in future?*

Wir wenden uns deshalb erneut an das Bun.en: We therefore turn once again to the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs and ask for concrete clarification.

Auf unsere bundesweiten Anfragen erreich.en: In response to our nationwide enquiries, we receive various replies from social courts.

Wir hatten die Gerichte insbesondere gef.en:
In particular, we had asked the courts:
- whether they know suitable experts for such assessments,
- whether they can provide guidance,
- and how those affected are supposed to find a suitable expert for an application under § 109 SGG.

Die eingehenden Antworten dokumentieren.en: We document the replies we receive on an ongoing basis. It is becoming increasingly clear that there is *no easily accessible, nationwide point of contact for those affected* through which the experts needed can be reliably found.

Wir wenden uns an das Bundesministerium.en: We turn to the federal ministry

Das Problem lässt sich nach unserer bish.en: According to our research so far, the problem cannot be solved through individual enquiries. That is why we send a comprehensive enquiry to the *Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs*.

Wir möchten insbesondere wissen:\n- Wie.en:
In particular, we want to know:
- How will it be ensured in future that those affected find suitable experts under § 109 SGG?
- Who will keep the planned register of expert assessors?
- What alternative is there as long as this register is not available?
- Can those affected at least get some guidance on which experts have already been used in comparable proceedings?

Für uns steht dabei nicht ein einzelnes.en: For us, the focus is not on a single expert opinion. It is about a *structural question of access to rights in social compensation law.*

Wir beginnen eine umfangreiche Recherche.en:
We begin extensive research with:
- social courts,
- medical associations,
- psychological and forensic-psychological professionals,
- professional associations,
- institutions,
- ministries,
- and other bodies.

Parallel fragen wir gezielt Sachverständ.en: At the same time, we specifically contact experts whose qualifications could in principle make them suitable for questions of testimony psychology or forensic psychology. The replies vary greatly.

Wir erfahren unter anderem:\n- Einige Fa.en:
Among other things, we learn:
- Some professionals do not prepare credibility assessments at all.
- Others only accept assignments from courts or authorities.
- Some do prepare such assessments, but are not available for privately initiated assessments.
- Others have no free capacity.
- Medical associations sometimes refer us to other associations, professional societies or psychological registers.
- For questions of testimony psychology, we are often referred to specially qualified forensic psychologists.

Damit wird genau das Spannungsfeld sicht.en: This makes visible exactly the tension that triggered our project: *Professionally suitable people exist – but that does not mean that those affected can actually name them for proceedings under § 109 SGG.*

Die Bundesstelle kann weiterhin niemande.en: The federal office still cannot name anyone

Nach erneuter Nachfrage bei der *Bundess.en: After another enquiry to the *Federal Office for Social Compensation (BfSE)*, we are told that there is no new information on the register of expert assessors. Even apart from this register, nobody there could name anyone to us for the kind of credibility assessment we are looking for.

Gleichzeitig erfahren wir, dass die Aufg.en: At the same time, we learn that the task of keeping this register is to be removed from the federal office’s remit as part of a change in the law.

Damit entsteht für uns eine neue Frage:.en: This raises a new question for us: *If the office responsible so far has not set up the register and the task is now being moved – who will make sure that those affected actually get access to suitable experts?*

Das vorgesehene Gutachterverzeichnis bef.en: The planned register of expert assessors is still “under development”

Bereits 2025 fragen wir bei der Bundesst.en: As early as 2025, we ask the Federal Office for Social Compensation about the register of expert assessors provided for in § 124 SGB XIV.

Uns wird mitgeteilt, dass sich die Umset.en: We are told that implementation is still under development. Due to extensive coordination, no specific date could be given for when the register would be available.

Damit beginnt für uns eine Recherche, di.en: This marks the start of research for us that was to go far beyond simply looking for a list.

Unser Projekt macht ein grundlegendes Sp.en: Our project makes a fundamental tension visible: on the one hand, in proceedings before the social courts there is a legal option *under § 109 SGG to have a particular doctor heard as an expert*.

Auf der anderen Seite kann gerade bei sp.en: On the other hand, especially for specific questions – for example an assessment of testimony credibility in connection with experiences of violence – finding a suitable person can be extremely difficult.

Hinzu kommt: Das im Sozialen Entschädigu.en: In addition: the register of expert assessors provided for in social compensation law was not yet available during our research.

Damit kann aus einem theoretisch vorhand.en: In this way, a right that exists in theory can become an obstacle in practice.

Was wir mit diesem Projekt erreichen möc.en: What we want to achieve with this project

Wir wollen nicht bei der Feststellung st.en:
We do not want to stop at stating that it is difficult. We want to make visible *where exactly the system does not work for those affected*. That is why we:
- document the replies of the responsible bodies,
- follow up with ministries and courts,
- collect possible points of contact,
- follow the development of the register of expert assessors,
- and draw attention to structural gaps.

Langfristig wünschen wir uns eine *trans.en: In the long term, we would like to see *transparent and nationwide guidance* that allows those affected to actually see: *Who is suitable for which assessment – and who is actually available for it?*

Denn ein Recht darf nicht davon abhängen.en: Because a right must not depend on whether a person affected has the strength, the knowledge and the means to search for a suitable professional themselves for months or years.

*Rechte müssen nicht nur bestehen. Sie m.en: *Rights must not only exist. They must also be within reach.*
